events_chronological: A boy is born in a small industrial town and grows into a weak, peculiar child.
His father throws him into the deep end of a pool to teach him to swim, and he sinks to the bottom.
He is conscripted as a chaplain's assistant and shipped overseas with no training worth the name.
He is lost behind the lines with a scout who beats him for wanting to be left to die.
The pair are captured, and the scout dies of gangrene on the prison train, blaming him with his last breath.
He is held in a camp beside enemy officers who have been drawing double rations for years through a clerical error.
He is sent on to a great city and housed with other prisoners in a disused abattoir.
The city is destroyed by fire in one night, and the prisoners in the meat locker come up to find it gone.
The prisoners are made to dig bodies out of the cellars until one of the diggers dies of the dry heaves.
A fellow prisoner promises to have him killed one day on the dead scout's account.
He comes home, collapses, and is hospitalised, where another patient introduces him to a hack science fiction writer.
He marries the daughter of the man who owns the optometry school and becomes rich.
He survives an air crash in the mountains, and his wife dies of exhaust fumes driving to the hospital.
He is taken by aliens and kept in a zoo on their planet with a film actress.
The aliens explain that every moment exists at once and that free will is an idea peculiar to his own planet.
He goes on a radio talk show and tries to tell the world about the aliens and the fourth dimension.
His daughter decides he is senile and takes his affairs out of his hands.
He is shot dead by a beam weapon after addressing a crowd, exactly as he has always known he would be.
nonlinear_category_reason: No timeline dominates, the scenes do not fall into two alternating bands, and no non-temporal principle groups them into blocks; the order is associative, so none of the other six shapes applies. A man unstuck in time is thrown between his childhood, the war, his optometry practice and an alien zoo with no warning and no pattern.
syuzhet_notes: The narration jumps without warning between the war, the marriage, the alien zoo and the death, often mid-paragraph and several times a page. It is not a frame with flashbacks and not two alternating strands; the sequence is associative and says so itself.
fabula_notes: The chronology is fully recoverable from ages, ranks and the fixed date of the firestorm, even though the telling refuses to set it out.

events.content: A physically slight and inward child grows up already ill-suited to the heroic masculinity his culture will later demand.

reader: the central figure begins life weak, peculiar and socially exposed

events.content: An attempted swimming lesson becomes passive near-drowning when the boy sinks and experiences the bottom as a place he need not leave.

reader: the protagonist's passivity before death begins in childhood

events.content: He enters war as a chaplain's assistant with neither combat preparation nor the temperament to imitate a soldier.

reader: the protagonist reaches the front almost completely unprepared

events.content: Lost behind the lines, the protagonist asks to be abandoned while the scout answers his surrender with blows and continued movement.

scout: the protagonist would rather stop than survive
reader: the protagonist responds to danger by yielding rather than fighting

events.content: A packed prison train carries them east; infection kills the scout while he fixes responsibility for his death on the man beside him.

reader: the capture creates a grievance that will outlive the war

questions.q75_6: who will carry the scout's final blame beyond his death?

events.content: Long-held officers appear healthy on accidental double rations, an absurd administrative abundance beside the exhausted arrivals.

reader: clerical error shapes survival even inside captivity

events.content: The protagonist's group is transferred into a great city and lodged below ground in a disused meat locker bearing a numbered address.

reader: the meat locker is the prisoners' shelter inside the city

questions.q75_1: where was he held immediately before the transfer to the city abattoir?

events.content: One night of incendiaries passes above the refrigerated cellar; morning reveals streets, buildings and inhabitants reduced almost entirely to ash.

protagonist: the city has been annihilated while the prisoners survived below
reader: the central wartime trauma is the destruction outside the meat locker

events.content: The survivors excavate sealed cellars until death from the dry heaves shows how even those spared by the bombing remain inside its aftermath.

reader: survival requires prolonged contact with the firestorm's dead

events.content: Accepting the dead scout's accusation, another prisoner turns it into a patient pledge that punishment will arrive even years later.

protagonist: someone intends to have him killed for the scout's death
reader: the war has planted a threat beyond its own end

events.content: Back in civilian life, he enters a hospital where another patient supplies strange books by a prolific speculative writer.

protagonist: the science-fiction books offer a language unlike ordinary war memory
reader: his postwar collapse follows the buried experience of the destroyed city

questions.q75_2: what happened overseas to leave him collapsed after returning home?

events.content: Marriage into a prosperous professional family gives him a practice, money and the outward shape of a stable life.
events.location: an optometry school and family home

reader: the protagonist acquires conventional postwar security

questions.q75_7: will the protagonist's prosperous domestic life remain intact?

events.content: Rescuers find him alive in mountain wreckage, while his panicked spouse dies from fumes during the drive to reach his hospital.

reader: chance again preserves the protagonist while killing someone near him

questions.q75_8: does surviving the crash allow him to escape the death he foresees?

events.content: He describes removal to another planet, where an actress shares a transparent enclosure and their private life becomes an exhibit.

reader: the protagonist claims direct experience of an alien world

questions.q75_5: what do the alien captors want him to understand about time?

events.content: They tell him every instant always exists and death is only attention fixed on a bad moment, removing choice from the universe they describe.

protagonist: all moments coexist and free will is a local illusion
reader: the novel's disordered chronology is also the protagonist's philosophy of time

events.content: A radio audience hears him present abduction and the fourth dimension as fact, exposing the private cosmology to public judgement.

reader: the protagonist no longer keeps the alien explanation private

events.content: She interprets his public certainty as senility and removes his practical independence while believing she is protecting him.

daughter: her father is publicly making impossible claims
reader: his family reads his temporal faith as incapacity

questions.q75_3: what convinced his daughter that he could no longer manage his own life?

events.content: After he lectures a crowd about the death he has always foreseen, a beam weapon fulfils the old prisoner's promise exactly on schedule.

reader: the foreknown death completes a revenge planted during captivity

questions.q75_4: why is the speaker assassinated at the death he predicted?
